_about: Optional inventory of IOS XE devices NOT registered in Catalyst Center. The IOS-XE MCP server reads this file (read-only) at startup and exposes it via the list_devices tool. Friendly `name` values can be passed as the `host` arg of show_command/config_command and will be resolved to the `host` IP/hostname here. NEVER put credentials in this file -- credentials come from IOS_XE_USERNAME/IOS_XE_PASSWORD (default profile) or IOS_XE_CRED_<NAME>_* (access profiles) in the environment only. All addresses below are RFC5737 documentation IPs (192.0.2.0/24); replace with your real management addresses.

dc-local.description: Example: DC devices with their own local account. Secrets come from IOS_XE_CRED_DC_USERNAME / IOS_XE_CRED_DC_PASSWORD.

legacy-telnet.description: Example: Telnet-only legacy devices (show commands only; needs IOS_XE_ALLOW_TELNET=true). Secrets come from IOS_XE_CRED_LEGACY_*.

devices.name: Site-A-Core1
devices.notes: Example: L3 super-core; HSRP-paired with Site-A-Core2. Demonstrates the `core` role and HSRP active/standby tags.

devices.name: Site-A-Core2
devices.notes: Example: L3 super-core; HSRP standby of Site-A-Core1.

devices.name: Site-A-Fusion
devices.notes: Example: Fusion router doing per-VRF route exchange with cores; demonstrates the `fusion` role, a per-site BGP AS that differs from the core AS, and an access profile with its own credential set.

devices.name: Site-A-Edge1
devices.notes: Example: SD-WAN edge serving as a DC anchor for a service VPN. Multiple VPN tags show how to mark which transports a device carries.

devices.name: Site-A-Edge2
devices.notes: Example: paired SD-WAN edge. Note this one does NOT carry VPN 130 -- this is exactly the kind of asymmetry the inventory is useful for surfacing.

devices.name: Branch-1-Edge1
devices.notes: Example: branch SD-WAN edge with an LTE backup transport.

devices.name: Site-Fabric-CP-BR-01
devices.notes: Example: SDA Control-Plane + Border (HA pair with -02). Devices like this are usually ALSO visible via Catalyst Center MCP -- inventory entries here are useful when you want a friendly name across both surfaces.

devices.name: Site-Fabric-WLC-01
devices.notes: Example: fabric-mode WLC. Demonstrates a non-router device type that still benefits from being listed here for friendly addressing.

devices.name: Lab-Router-01
devices.notes: Example of a disabled entry: the device exists in the topology but the inventory record needs more work (placeholder management IP, role under review, etc.). list_devices(...) will skip enabled=false entries by default; pass enabled=null to include them.
